examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Convert RPM to revolution time using 60/RPM seconds; average rotational latency is half a revolution. Add seek, rotational wait and actual transfer, using the access model given. Random sectors may each incur rotational wait; contiguous transfers often amortize it. Disk scheduling head movement is not the same as elapsed service time.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A disk rotates at 12000 RPM and has 1000 sectors per track. What is transfer time for one sector in microseconds, ignoring seek and latency?

**Answer: 5.** A revolution takes 60/12000=0.005 s=5000 μs. At 1000 sectors per track, one sector passes in 5000/1000=5 μs.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An average rotational delay of 2500 μs would be added only if requested. Do not confuse that waiting delay with the 5 μs sector-transfer time.

SCAN and LOOK can produce different totals because SCAN may travel to the disk endpoint.
